theme: A liquid that must do four things at once
title: Solvent Blend and Sacrificial Additive Under a Window-Decomposition Cliff
strategies: trivial: 100% of the single native-safest solvent (highest anodic threshold), zero additive -- the checker's own reference construction

greedy: pure conductivity/viscosity trade-off optimizer -- rank solvents by kappa/eta and use 100% of the single best one, never touching the additive library or modeling the electrochemical window at all (the trap: this solvent decomposes whenever its native threshold sits below the instance's target window)

strong: decoupling search -- for every candidate primary solvent, either use it bare (if natively safe) or dose the cheapest reachable additive subset just far enough to hit the required SEI coverage, rescuing a low-viscosity/high-conductivity solvent that would otherwise fail the window check instead of retreating to the safe-but-slow solvent

open ceiling (uncovered): joint multi-solvent blending, salt-concentration tuning, and globally optimal (non-greedy-ordered) additive-subset dosing under the ratio objective -- strong only searches single-primary-solvent blends
